root_cause.text: In ASoC soc-core, `snd_soc_unbind_card()` only flushed `close_delayed_work` before `soc_cleanup_card_resources()`, but `snd_card_disconnect_sync()` inside cleanup could still trigger PCM close paths that reschedule delayed DAPM work after the flush, letting `soc_remove_link_components()` free DAPM widgets before `snd_soc_dapm_stream_event()` runs and causing a use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `snd_soc_flush_all_delayed_work(card);` inside `soc_cleanup_card_resources()` specifically “after `snd_card_disconnect_sync()`” and “before `soc_remove_link_dais()` and `soc_remove_link_components()`,” and the CVE text explains that PCM close during cleanup can call `snd_soc_dapm_stream_stop()` to schedule new delayed work that the earlier flush in `snd_soc_unbind_card()` misses.

intent_record.intent_summary: Flush delayed sound card work before tearing down DAIs and DAPM widgets to avoid teardown-order races.
intent_record.what: A call to `snd_soc_flush_all_delayed_work(card);` was inserted in `soc_cleanup_card_resources(struct snd_soc_card *card)` immediately after the loop that exits initialized rtd links and before the code that removes DAIs and DAPM widgets. A comment was added describing that delayed work is flushed before removing DAIs and DAPM widgets.
intent_record.how: At runtime, any pending delayed work associated with the sound card is forced to complete or be canceled before the card's DAIs and DAPM widgets are torn down. This reduces the chance that deferred work will run against resources that are in the process of being removed, preventing use-after-free or other teardown ordering issues.

grouping_result.intent: Flush delayed sound card work before tearing down DAIs and DAPM widgets to avoid teardown-order races.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the vulnerability root cause: it adds flushing of delayed sound card work before DAI/DAPM teardown to prevent teardown-order races and the resulting use-after-free.

candidates.rationale: This frees link components and associated DAPM widgets during card teardown. According to the root cause, cleanup can still trigger PCM close paths that reschedule delayed DAPM work, so freeing components here before that work runs creates the use-after-free.

vuln_statements.explanation: This teardown call frees link components and associated DAPM widgets. Per the root cause, delayed PCM close activity can still be triggered during cleanup after the earlier work flush, and any rescheduled DAPM work may then run after these widgets have been freed, causing a use-after-free.
